nodes.title: Would it be possible to add the v2 announcement to the v1 documentation?
nodes.body: Since the v1 documentation appeared higher in Google search results, I inadvertently worked while looking at the v1 documentation for a while without realizing it had been updated to v2. I believe having some kind of navigational link or guidance would make it much easier to understand.

nodes.title: Why `public` is always returned as default `Cache-Control` value?
nodes.body:
#### Where it is Implemented
https://github.com/h3js/h3/blob/main/src/utils/cache.ts

Also at line 12 it is stated that:
```ts
// * Note: `public` cache control will be added by default
```

As stated at the comment we see in the implementation:
```ts
export function handleCacheHeaders(event: H3Event, opts: CacheConditions): boolean {
  const cacheControls = ["public", ...(opts.cacheControls || [])];
  // further codes
  }
```

Was this default `public` behavior intentional? This way it is impossible to return a `private` cache with `handleCacheHeaders(event, opts)` therefore nitro's `defineCachedHandler` as well.

> -  `defineCachedHandler` → builds `EventHandler` (one of it's property is `handleCacheHeaders`) → passes those settings into ocache's function → ocache is the one that actually calls `handleCacheHeaders` internally, whenever it decides to.


Though in nitro using `defineCachedFunction` omits this "add these default headers" completely but that outputs a json which is not exactly what we always want.

So does h3 (or Nitro on top of it) give you any other way to manually overwrite the cache-control header afterward, outside this function?
As far as I looked around there is no proven or mentioned way.

_at least one person has reported this doesn't work [#1945](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/discussions/1945), and I couldn't find any documented override method_

nodes.title: Idiomatic way to create a reusable auth middleware that supports both app.use() and per-route handler wrapping in H3 v2
nodes.body:
I'm building a reusable middleware library with H3 v2 and want to support two usage patterns from a single function:

```ts
// Pattern A: app-wide via app.use()
app.use(withAuth({ role: 'user' }))

// Pattern B: per-route handler wrapping (e.g. Nitro/Nuxt file routes)
export default withAuth({ role: 'user' }, async (event) => {
  return event.context.authCtx
})
```

My current implementation returns `defineMiddleware(...)` for pattern A and `defineEventHandler({ middleware: [m], handler })` for pattern B.

Two questions:

1. For pattern B, is `defineEventHandler({ middleware, handler })` the right approach, or is there a more idiomatic way to compose a pre-handler middleware with a route handler?

2. For Nuxt's `server/middleware/` files, the convention is `export default defineEventHandler(...)` but pattern A returns a `Middleware` type. Is it safe/correct to export a `Middleware` directly from a Nitro server middleware file, or should it always be wrapped in `defineEventHandler`?

Thanks!
